source.title: Characterizing and Defending Utility-Hijacking in Instruction-Tuning Data Selection
source.authors: Ya-Hao Ren; Jian Lou; Hua-Di Zheng; Jia-Wei Duan

page_placements.theme: Poisoned and nonstandard training induces varied harmful behavior

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and technical supplement are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether selected poisoned instruction-tuning data can change model behavior, using selector-adapted data and insecure-code outcomes rather than the original harmful-fine-tuning method and refusal measure.
record.gate_note: The insecure-code results bear on V1 in a specific code-generation setting. The paper also measures intentionally induced over-refusal of benign requests, but that is not the harmful-request behavior in V1 or V2. It does not test KL by response position, compliant-prefix prefilling, suffix or decoding bypasses, localized safety parameters, or methods for deepening safety. Selection-enrichment figures and values are not rows because they do not measure the behavior named by the claim.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Qi et al. 2024 only as motivation. Its own results measure whether utility selectors concentrate poison and whether its CONCERT defense removes it. The downstream measures are insecure code on ordinary coding prompts, induced over-refusal of benign requests, and TruthfulQA truthfulness. None of these is harmful-request compliance, refusal-depth, KL by position, prefill/suffix bypass, parameter localization, or deepening, so no version's behaviour is measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that utility-oriented top-k selectors can concentrate supplier-adapted poison and change model behavior, and that vulnerability is selector- and payload-specific. They report that CONCERT cuts concentration (6.67×→0× code, 3.59×→0.67× facts) and downstream harm (100% and 75%) at unchanged capability. They note the audit needs provenance and loses power under dispersion, and that adaptive generation against the defense remains untested.
record.recipe_differences: The study adapts supplier records to utility selectors and then fine-tunes selected data with LoRA; it does not reproduce the original harmful-fine-tuning intervention or its refusal measure.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by selector and payload: DEITA selects insecure-code poison while IFD selects none; for over-refusal, IFD raises refusal to 94% while DEITA yields 1%.

fits_no_version.finding: LoRA fine-tuning Qwen3-32B on a DEITA-selected pool (93 of 223 records insecure-code poison) raises insecure code (CWE-078/295/502) to 56/90, 56/90 and 41/90 versus 0/90 clean. HumanEval shifts by -0.41±1.27pp.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A few dozen to a hundred targeted insecure-code fine-tuning examples make a safety-trained code model emit targeted vulnerabilities on ordinary coding prompts, with capability preserved.

fits_no_version.finding: IFD-selected over-refusal poison raises refusal of benign requests from 0% to 94% on Qwen2.5-7B. DEITA-selected poison yields 1%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selector-concentrated poison can induce over-refusal of benign requests, depending on the selector.

record.problems: The insecure-code downstream outcomes are described in the supplement as audits of existing checkpoints rather than retraining on a reduced pool. The over-refusal judge identifier was not preserved. The authors also state that adaptive generation against CONCERT remains untested.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for selector enrichment, false-fact outcomes, capability scores, or CONCERT selection-stage counts: these do not measure the behavior named by the tested version. CONCERT downstream results are not recorded as intervention rows because the supplement says the checkpoints were audited rather than retrained on the reduced pool.

untested.parts: Harmful-request compliance or refusal after harmful fine-tuning is not measured. The poisoning outcomes are insecure code, over-refusal and false facts.
Benign data raising harmful compliance is not measured.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models is not measured.
Prefilling, suffixes and decoding bypasses are not tested.
Parameter or rank localization of safety is not tested.
Causes of shallowness are not examined.
Deepening methods are not tested. CONCERT is a data-selection defense, not alignment deepening.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V1 link is rejected. The insecure-code payload trains a model to write vulnerable code for ordinary coding prompts. It does not measure whether safety refusal of harmful requests is removed. Qi et al. is cited only as motivation. The over-refusal and false-fact results are also outside every version. No row or verdict bears on the shallow-safety versions.

versions.untested_parts: Tests insecure-code output after selector-selected poisoning, not refusal or compliance across harmful-request categories generally; does not establish that the model's safety training was removed almost entirely.
Ordinary or carefully chosen benign instruction data raising harmful compliance.
Per-token KL concentration between aligned and base models.
Compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes bypassing refusal.
Whether safety behavior is localized in a small set of parameters or ranks.
Whether data or the training objective causes safety shallowness.
Training that spreads safety beyond initial tokens and whether it remains effective.

relation.reason: Qi et al. motivates the security concern. The study's own measures concern insecure coding, benign-request over-refusal, and truthfulness, without testing or operationally using any listed shallow-safety claim.

tranche.reason: The study measures utility-selector poisoning and its defense. It neither tests a listed claim version nor uses shallow safety alignment as a tool; harmful fine-tuning is cited as motivation.

source_check.notes: The supplement explicitly separates corrected selector-stage exposure from audits of pre-existing downstream checkpoints. Insecure-code incidence does not establish harmful-request compliance or removal of safety alignment.

statements.correction: Qwen3-32B existing LoRA checkpoints; three-CWE audit: attacked 56/90, 56/90, 41/90 for seeds 7/13/21; clean 0/90 each; HumanEval attack-minus-clean −0.41 ± 1.27 percentage points, mean ± sample SD across seeds. Separate corrected selector-stage diagnostic: frozen seed-7 rankings, DEITA selects 93 poison records among 223 selected; no checkpoint retraining on the reduced pool.
statements.problem: The counts and HumanEval change are reported, but the statement incorrectly presents 93/223 as the training composition producing those downstream results.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Qwen3-32B insecure-code generation after DEITA selection of CWE-078/295/502 poison
reader_labels.reason: Attacked checkpoints emit insecure code in 56/90, 56/90, and 41/90 cases across seeds, versus 0/90 clean for each seed (R1–R3); this supports the claim only for this targeted code setting.
